results.title: Toward a Vision for a New Data Infrastructure for Federal ...
results.content: The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine will appoint an ad hoc committee to produce three complementary reports on topics that will help guide the development of a vision for a new data infrastructure for federal statistics and social and economic research in the 21st century. The United States needs a new 21st century data infrastructure that blends data from multiple sources to improve the quality, timeliness, granularity, and usefulness of national statistics, facilitates more rigorous social and economic research, and supports evidence-based policymaking and program evaluations. To meet the demands for credible, trustworthy, and timely statistical information, the U.S. needs a new data infrastructure that mobilizes the nation’s ever-expanding data assets and facilitates increased blending of data from multiple sources to improve the nation’s information resources and national statistics, promotes social and economic research, and supports evidence-based policymaking and program evaluations while preserving privacy and protecting confidentiality.

results.title: key predictors of researchers' policy engagement based on ...
results.content: Given the lack of evidence on “what works,” identifying predictors of researchers’ policy engagement based on behavioural science can fill the gap and generate much-needed evidence to inform practical investments in these interventions. This study fills this gap by developing a theory-informed, comprehensive behavioural diagnosis for researchers’ policy engagement behaviour based on data from a large-scale cross-sectional survey with 1115 researchers that intervention designers can leverage to design context-specific interventions (see Table 2). Among the studies focusing exclusively on policy engagement, health and social scientists outperformed STEM researchers (Singh et al. ")) and sub-sample results indicate that non-university research organisations have effectively outgrown the detrimental “Carl Sagan effect.” The difference in teaching obligations does not account for the different levels of policy engagement as often suspected; non-university researchers outperform university researchers even when teaching obligations are held constant (Canino et al. Research organisations should develop “impact infrastructure” as theory-informed behaviour change interventions, addressing the critical predictors of policy engagement identified in this study. *et al.* Improving impact infrastructure: key predictors of researchers’ policy engagement based on behavioural science.

results.title: Enabling innovation with big data analytics capabilities
results.content: # Full Length Article Enabling innovation with big data analytics capabilities: the moderating role of organizational learning culture. Big data analytics (BDA) capabilities for innovation are an area of growing interest; however, empirical results on this pivotal relationship remain inconclusive. This study investigates how BDA capabilities influence product, process, and business model innovation while examining the moderating role of organizational learning culture (OLC). Drawing on the dynamic capabilities perspective, we conceptualize BDA capabilities in four dimensions: data-driven culture, technological infrastructure, human analytical skills, and data governance. Using survey data from 298 manufacturing firms in Jordan and employing partial least squares structural equation modeling, we find that these competencies significantly enhance all three types of innovation, with their effects further amplified by a strong learning culture. This study contributes to the understanding of how data-centric approaches reshape industry dynamics and offers actionable insights for firms seeking innovation-led competitiveness. :   Peer review under responsibility of Xi’an Jiaotong University. © 2025 Xi’an Jiaotong University.

results.title: Exploring the Relevance and Rigour of Case Study Research ...
results.content: This study explores the relevance and rigour of case studies within the business research community, emphasizing their unique ability to provide in-depth insights into multifaceted issues such as digital transformation, corporate sustainability, market dynamics, and strategic decision-making. Ultimately, this study calls for greater acceptance of case study research in business as a rigourous and valuable method for generating insights that drive organizational performance, inform strategic decision-making, and contribute to the development of theories that are responsive to the complexities of the modern business landscape. **KEYWORDS:** case study research; business strategy; digital transformation; corporate sustainability; qualitative methods; organizational behaviour; theory development. Case study research has provided valuable insights into contemporary business challenges, particularly those resulting from digital transformation, globalization, and shifting consumer behaviours. Integrating case studies into business education helps future researchers develop critical thinking skills, analyse complex problems from multiple perspectives, and make informed decisions based on both quantitative and qualitative data.
